recent_articles.title: Assam, Meghalaya farmers resume farming in disputed border area after weeks of conflict - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Villagers** in Assam and Meghalaya resumed farming activities in a disputed border area after weeks of intermittent conflict. The resumption followed an agreement brokered by representatives from the two state governments, who met on Tuesday to resolve the dispute in the Tapat-Lapangap sector. **Deimonmi Lyngdoh**, head of Lapangap's traditional community organization, expressed hope that this temporary arrangement would strengthen relations and contribute towards a lasting resolution of border issues.  This agreement is part of a larger effort to resolve 12 disputed sectors along their 855-kilometer border since 1972.

recent_articles.title: Meghalaya and Nagaland CMs call for release of 20 hostages - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Meghalaya** and **Nagaland** Chief Ministers have called for the early release of 20 civilians, including 14 Kukis and six Nagas, allegedly held hostage by armed groups in Manipur. **Conrad K. Sangma**, Meghalaya's Chief Minister, expressed concern over the continued captivity of the villagers and urged all parties to pursue dialogue instead of violence. **Neiphiu Rio**, Nagaland's Chief Minister, also contacted **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister, expressing his concern over the abduction of six Liangmai Nagas.  **Mr. Shah** assured him that necessary measures would be taken to secure their release and bring the perpetrators to justice.

recent_articles.title: BJP Core Group Meet At PM Modi's Residence Today, Rajya Sabha Polls On Agenda
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** top leaders, including Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, JP Nadda, and party president Nitin Nabin, will meet at **Prime Minister Narendra Modi's** residence this evening to discuss the upcoming Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections. The meeting will focus on finalizing candidates for these elections, which are scheduled for June 18th, as well as strategizing for the high-stakes Rajya Sabha polls following the recent defeat of the Women's reservation bill.  The party also plans to discuss strengthening its organization, mobilizing supporters, and highlighting achievements of the Modi government over the past twelve years.

recent_articles.title: India's Exercise PRAGATI: Troops From Many Nations Train To Fight Together
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** hosted a joint military exercise, PRAGATI 2026, involving soldiers from 13 countries including Bhutan, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Seychelles, Sri Lanka, and Vietnam. The two-week training focused on counter-terrorism, jungle warfare, rappelling, and casualty evacuation drills, with troops operating in mixed groups to enhance coordination for real-time emergency responses.  The exercise highlighted the shared security challenges faced by these nations, including terrorism, crossborder crimes, maritime threats, disaster management, and regional instability.

recent_articles.title: Multilateral joint military exercise in Meghalaya focuses on counter-insurgency, building trust - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Thirteen** countries, including Bhutan, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Seychelles, Sri Lanka, Vietnam and India, concluded the maiden multilateral military exercise 'Pragati 2026' in Meghalaya. The two-week exercise focused on countering insurgency and building mutual trust among nations in the Indian Ocean region.  **Brigadier Mayur Shekatkar**, chief coordinator of the program, stated that the exercise provided a platform for building friendship and camaraderie among participating nations through sports and cultural activities. **Col. Sandeep Poonia**, director of the exercise, emphasized the importance of sharing best practices and enhancing interoperability to ensure a stable and secure region.

recent_articles.title: Disambiguating a year of flux: expert panels at The Hindu Huddle, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of The Hindu Group's ideas conclave, The Hindu Huddle, will be held in Bengaluru on June 5 and 6, 2026.  **Siddaramaiah**, **D.K. Shivakumar**, and other Chief Ministers from across the country will participate alongside Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship **Jayant Chaudhary**, **Omar Abdullah**, **A. Revanth Reddy**, and **K.G. Arunraj**. The event will feature discussions on topics such as tariffs' impact on the Indian economy, diplomacy in managing crises, and artificial intelligence's influence on various aspects of life.  **The Hindu Huddle** is presented by the Sami-Sabinsa Group and co-powered by the Government of Telangana.

recent_articles.title: Public hearing for limestone mining called off in Meghalaya after protest - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Jaiñtia National Council, Hima Sutnga Youth Federation, Jaiñtia Students' Union
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The authorities in Meghalaya’s East Jaiñtia Hills district canceled a public hearing for a ₹1,800-crore integrated cement plant and limestone mining project after two groups clashed. Supporters of the project and those opposed to it engaged in violence, including the burning of a truck, leaving several people injured. The conflict followed similar clashes on Thursday near the District Magistrate’s office, where police used batons to disperse the groups.  The **Jaiñtia National Council**, **Hima Sutnga Youth Federation**, and **Jaiñtia Students’ Union** stormed the public hearing site, leading to its cancellation.

recent_articles.title: Public hearing for limestone mining called off in Meghalaya after protest - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The authorities in Meghalaya’s East Jaiñtia Hills district canceled a public hearing for a ₹1,800-crore integrated cement plant and limestone mining project after two groups clashed. Supporters of the project and opponents faced off at Lum Syrman, resulting in a truck being set ablaze and minor injuries to some people. The incident followed a similar clash near the District Magistrate’s office on Thursday, prompting police intervention.

recent_articles.title: Reble's Praying Mantis: The female rapper reshaping Indian hip-hop
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Reble**, a rapper from Meghalaya, India, has gained significant popularity with her unique blend of English and indigenous languages. Her breakout moment came with the Bollywood film *Dhurandhar*, where her music resonated with audiences.  Her latest single, "Praying Mantis," continues to generate discussion online. **Reble**'s rise reflects a broader shift in Indian pop culture towards embracing regional artists. Despite facing criticism for her style and lyrics, she remains committed to her artistic vision and believes consistency is key to success.

recent_articles.title: Meghalaya: Looking beyond the grape | Market demand for fruit wines and an enabling government policy is motivating small-time winemakers to go commercial - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lyang B. Sangma**, an entrepreneur from Meghalaya, is excited about the potential of his te.gism fruit wine after it was selected by the **Meghalaya Farmers Empowerment Commission (MFEC)** to be showcased at Vinexpo India 2024 in Mumbai. The MFEC chose six exotic fruit wines and meads for the event, including Sangma's te.gism product, which has gained recognition from experts and connoisseurs beyond his hometown of Tura.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Shree Cement shares jump 4% even as Q4 profit drops 8%. Why Nomura, Elara, other brokerages remain bullish - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Shree Cement's** shares surged 4% on Thursday after the company reported a 10% revenue increase and a 97% jump in net profit for the January-March quarter of its financial year 2026. The cement giant saw total sales volume grow by 11% year-on-year, with a 27% rise in revenue from operations compared to the previous year's quarter. **Nomura**, **JM Financial**, and **Elara Capital** all maintained their positive ratings on the company's stock, citing strong performance and growth potential.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Why is India turning to crocodiles and snakes to ‘fence’ Bangladesh border? | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Indian** Border Security Force (BSF) is exploring the use of apex predators like crocodiles and venomous snakes to deter undocumented migration along its border with **Bangladesh**.  This controversial plan, aimed at addressing challenging terrain that makes traditional fencing difficult, has raised concerns from human rights activists and wildlife conservationists. The BSF's directive to explore this option comes despite the fact that these animals are not native to the region and could pose a threat to local ecosystems and communities. Critics argue that deploying such measures is inhumane and ineffective, highlighting the government's use of fear tactics against undocumented migrants. This approach has been compared to similar controversial strategies employed in the United States, including proposals for using alligators or snakes to deter migrants.

recent_articles.title: Honeymoon murder: Meghalaya court reserves order on bail plea of key accused - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Raj Kushwaha**, one of the key suspects in the murder of **Raja Raghuvanshi**, a businessman from Indore, is awaiting a decision on his bail plea.  The **Meghalaya** court reserved its order after hearing arguments from Kushwaha's counsel, who stated that all evidence has been presented. Sonam, **Raghuvanshi's** wife and another accused, was granted bail earlier this week. The case involves the alleged murder of **Raghuvanshi** during his honeymoon in Meghalaya last year.

recent_articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Girotra**, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  **Ashok Sengupta**, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. **Isaac Kehimkar**, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

recent_articles.title: Constitution Amendment Bill proposes possible change in size of State Assemblies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Constitution** (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes significant changes to State Legislative Assemblies by restarting the delimitation process and removing a long-standing constitutional freeze on seat readjustments. The bill aims to update constituency boundaries based on population changes and will be introduced in a Special Session of Parliament beginning April 16th.  The Delimitation Commission, chaired by a former or sitting Supreme Court judge, will determine the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and redraw parliamentary and Assembly constituencies. Public consultation on draft proposals will precede finalization before the new boundaries take effect for elections after the Commission's final orders are published in the Gazette of India.

recent_articles.title: Meghalaya yields new burrowing reed snake - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A team of researchers from multiple institutions, including **Help Earth**, **Cotton University**, and the **Zoological Survey of India**, have described a new species of burrowing reed snake called *Calamaria garoensis* found in Meghalaya's West Garo Hills district. The study, published in Taprobanica, confirmed that this species is distinct from other related species based on morphological examination and mitochondrial DNA analysis.  The discovery highlights the rich biodiversity of the region and emphasizes the need for further research and conservation efforts to protect these often overlooked creatures.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The **Election Commission** has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

recent_articles.title: On Assam campaign trail, Meghalaya CM stresses ‘One Northeast’ mission - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Conrad K. Sangma**, Meghalaya's Chief Minister, reaffirmed his "One Northeast" mission during campaigning for the National People's Party (NPP) candidate in Assam.  He emphasized the NPP's goal of unified representation across the region to strengthen the northeast's voice at various levels and highlighted the launch of the One Northeast political platform in November 2025, which he co-founded with others like **Pradyot Bikram Manikya Debbarma** of the Tipra Motha Party, **Mmhonlumo Kikon**, a former BJP legislator from Nagaland, and **Daniel Langthasa**.  The NPP has fielded three candidates in Assam's April 9 elections.

recent_articles.title: Cow, buffalo for each Assam tribal family, promises Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister** and senior **BJP** leader, promised to give a cow and a buffalo to each tribal family in Assam if the party is re-elected for a third consecutive term. He also pledged to establish large dairies in every district and highlighted the BJP's commitment to indigenous people through increased funding for their welfare.  Shah attributed the rise in budget allocation for indigenous peoples to Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, while emphasizing that the BJP has been proactive in addressing tribal concerns, including clashes between infiltrators and local tribes. He also promised to introduce a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) to curb polygamy and population growth among infiltrators.

recent_articles.title: AI, shifting industries are redefining careers: Market experts - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Anoop Mehta**, president of **Bharat Diamond Bourse**, and **Vijay Kedia**, managing director of **Kedia Securities**, spoke at the 17th annual convocation of the **Indian Institute of Management-Shillong**. They emphasized the importance of adaptability and continuous self-improvement in a rapidly changing world, driven by advancements in AI and shifting industries.  **Shishir Kumar Bajoria**, chairman of the Board of Governors, highlighted the unique learning environment of the northeastern region while **Professor Naliniprava Tripathy**, director of IIM-Shillong, presented the institute's annual report which included seven new international collaborations and progress towards AACSB and EQUIS accreditations.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: ‘Stree Nidhi’ to take up staff recruitment soon: Seethakka - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Stree Nidhi Credit Cooperative Federation Limited
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Danasari Anasuya**, **Minister of Panchayati Raj and Rural Development**, announced government approval for 163 new appointments at the Stree Nidhi Credit Cooperative Federation Limited.  She also praised the federation's growth, noting its strong financial position with a loan portfolio exceeding ₹5,500 crore. The Minister highlighted the federation's success in expanding digital access and enabling post office cash transactions in remote areas.

recent_articles.title: Comprehensively review maintenance standards at UNESCO sites: Parliamentary panel to govt - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A Parliamentary panel has recommended to the **Ministry of Culture** that it undertake a comprehensive review of maintenance standards and visitor facilities at all UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India, coordinating with the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**. The panel also urged the Ministry to prepare a five-year UNESCO nomination strategy, including a pipeline of at least 10 potential nominations, a structured engagement plan for multinational nominations, and dedicated staff and budgetary provision for preparing nomination dossiers.  The Ministry is expected to present this strategy within one year and furnish final utilization figures for 2025-26 within 90 days. The panel noted that India's growing portfolio of UNESCO World Heritage Sites carries with it a corresponding obligation under the UNESCO Operational Guidelines to maintain standards of conservation, interpretation, and visitor management commensurate with their global recognition.

recent_articles.title: Lone rangers flex their muscle against alliances in Assam battle - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF)** and **United People’s Party Liberation (UPPL)** are confident about their performance in the upcoming Assam Assembly elections, with both parties aiming to significantly increase their seat share.  These non-aligned parties have been gaining momentum as the election date approaches, potentially disrupting the anticipated straight fight between the Bharatiya Janata Party-led NDA and the Congress-led ASM. The AIUDF, which won 16 seats in 2021, is contesting most of its seats in Muslim-dominated areas, while the UPPL, which won six seats in 2021, is contesting more seats outside its core area.  Other non-aligned parties include the Trinamool Congress, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, Aam Aadmi Party, and the National People’s Party.

recent_articles.title: After GHADC amendment, Meghalaya groups seek curbs on non-tribal voters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Four tribal groups** in Meghalaya have petitioned **Meghalaya Governor Chandrashekhar H. Vijayshankar** requesting similar measures to bar non-tribal people from voting in elections to tribal councils. The petition, submitted on March 24, 2026, argues that such measures are necessary to protect the constitutional intent of these councils and safeguard the rights of indigenous tribes. **Deputy Chief Minister Prestone Tynsong** has stated that the Meghalaya government will ask other tribal councils in the state to adopt the GHADC model. The GHADC election was postponed after violence erupted between tribal and non-tribal groups.

recent_articles.title: Meghalaya leader of Opposition Mukul Sangma demands independent inquiry into Garo Hills violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mukul Sangma**, leader of the Opposition in Meghalaya, urged **Governor C.H. Vijayashankar** to establish an independent commission of inquiry into the Garo Hills violence.  Sangma cited a series of events linked to the tribal Garo Hills Autonomous District Council (GHADC) elections as contributing factors to the unrest, including demands by civil society organizations and alleged actions by former officials. He expressed concern over police action, alleging random arrests without proper verification. Sangma called for an investigation into the violence's causes, identification of responsible parties, and accountability for any government failures.  He also emphasized the need for continued dialogue to resolve the issue and restore peace in Meghalaya.

recent_articles.title: 33 detained Bangladeshi nationals sent back from Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nearly 33 Bangladeshi immigrants**, detained in Tamil Nadu's Salem district, were transported by train to West Bengal on March 20, 2026.  The operation was carried out with the assistance of the **Railway Protection Force (RPF)** and **Border Security Force (BSF)** personnel. The immigrants will be sent back to Bangladesh through the border after being handed over by the Tamil Nadu police. This follows an ongoing drive launched by the **Ministry of Home Affairs** a couple of years ago, aimed at deporting undocumented Bangladeshi nationals from various states.

recent_articles.title: One more arrested in West Bengal in Osman Hadi murder case; total held rises to three - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
## Bangladesh Leader's Murder: Third Arrest Made in West Bengal

A third suspect has been arrested in connection with the murder of popular Bangladeshi leader Osman Hadi. Philip Sangma, a border tout operating between India and Bangladesh, was apprehended by the State police’s Special Task Force on Saturday. Sangma admitted to facilitating Faisal and Alamgir, two suspects already in custody, into India.  He also confessed to helping them cross the border illegally. This arrest follows the apprehension of Faisal and Alamgir last week near the border between West Bengal and Bangladesh. The investigation revealed that Sangma himself crossed over to India after pressure mounted on him.
